summary:
Paraná is a state of Brazil and stands under the national framework carried by the parent record; the findings below are specific to the state and its municipalities.

Access to sex-separated facilities has been contested in Paraná's own legislature and in municipal councils. In 2021 state representative Mara Lima introduced a bill prohibiting unisex bathrooms statewide and requiring separate male and female facilities. On 16 November 2021 the Curitiba City Council approved a municipal bill of the same kind, introduced by councilman Ezequias Barros. The inventory does not record whether either measure was enacted.

On 4 October 2023 the Curitiba City Council approved, by symbolic vote, a motion of protest against Resolution 2/2023 of the federal Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship, issued on 19 September 2023, which provided that educational institutions must guarantee use of bathrooms, changing rooms and other gender-segregated spaces according to each student's gender identity and expression, while recommending additional individual-use bathrooms in public spaces. The Ministry stated that the resolution has no binding effect and that no school is obliged to adopt it. The Curitiba motion was to be converted into an official letter to the federal government.

Gender markers on documents issued in the state are governed by the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná. In 2023 that court published a provision guaranteeing inclusion of a non-binary option in the Civil Registry gender marker, then revoked it in November 2023, limiting administrative replacement of first name and sex to male and female only. In 2025 the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná authorized a third gender option on documents.

Trans participation in sport has produced conflicting rulings between a municipality and the national courts. On 26 April 2024 Londrina enacted a law banning transgender people from competing in sports according to gender identity, with a R$10,000 fine for non-compliance. On 26 February 2026 the Londrina City Council approved a motion to bar transgender athlete Tiffanny Abreu from the Brazilian Women's Volleyball Cup; the Brazilian Volleyball Confederation filed suit in the Supreme Federal Court and Justice Cármen Lúcia issued a preliminary injunction the same day allowing her to compete. In March 2026 LGBTQ rights organizations filed suit against the Londrina law in the Supreme Federal Court, and on 7 August 2026 rapporteur Justice Cristiano Zanin voted to strike the law down. The inventory does not record a final judgment.

Relationship recognition in Paraná was established before the national rule took effect. On 26 March 2013 the General Inspector of Justice of Paraná ruled that same-sex marriage and the conversion of stable unions to marriage must use normal marriage procedures, and same-sex civil marriage was authorized in all cartórios statewide under the same procedure and documentation as heterosexual marriage, with conversion of a stable union into marriage permitted without judicial authorization. In 2004 Curitiba recorded the first recognition of a same-sex union in Brazil: common-law marriage status, previously limited to opposite-sex couples, for an English-Brazilian couple who had cohabited fourteen years.

State courts have granted adoption to same-sex couples. On 14 May 2009 the 2nd Court of Childhood, Youth and Adoption granted the first gay-couple adoption in Paraná to a Curitiba couple, finding a stable and affectionate union able to raise a child in a healthy environment. On 27 October 2010 Judge Sergio Luiz Kreuz in Cascavel authorized irreversible adoption of an eight-year-old child with cerebral palsy by a gay couple together twelve years, under Superior Court of Justice precedent. On 16 September 2011 Maringá justice authorized adoption of two children by a lesbian couple.
tangentialFactors:
The Court of Justice of the State of Paraná moved in opposite directions within two years on the same question: a non-binary civil registry marker was published in 2023, withdrawn in November 2023 in favour of male and female only, and a third gender option on documents was authorized in 2025. The inventory does not reconcile the two positions or state which one governs applications filed today.

The Londrina sports ban and the Curitiba facilities measures are municipal acts that conflict with positions later taken by national courts and with a federal resolution the Curitiba council protested. Enforcement exposure therefore turns on which instrument a given authority applies; the inventory records litigation and injunctions rather than settled outcomes.

The inventory contains no documented incident of violence against a trans or travesti person in Paraná, and no state-level count of such incidents. Nothing in it supports a comparison of Paraná's violence risk with other states.
localsOnly:
Residents of Curitiba live under a municipal prohibition on unisex bathrooms approved on 16 November 2021, and the state legislature has before it a statewide bill of the same kind introduced in 2021; the inventory does not record the current status of either measure.

Registry practice for residents shifted twice: name and sex replacement was limited to male and female in November 2023, and a third gender option on documents was authorized by the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná in 2025.

Organisers and competitors in Londrina face a municipal law of 26 April 2024 carrying a R$10,000 fine for allowing transgender athletes to compete according to gender identity, subject to litigation at the Supreme Federal Court in which a preliminary injunction of 26 February 2026 permitted Tiffanny Abreu to compete and a rapporteur vote of 7 August 2026 favoured striking the law down.

Same-sex couples in the state have obtained marriage, union conversion and adoption through ordinary state procedures since 2013, with adoption rulings in Curitiba, Cascavel and Maringá on record.
